ucs.title: [LLM] Akira ransomware shadow copy deletion via PowerShell WMI (Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject)
ucs.description: Hunts the verbatim PowerShell one-liner that Akira (Howling Scorpius / PUNK SPIDER / GOLD SAHARA) consistently runs immediately before encryption to defeat VSS-based recovery. CISA AA24-109A and Mandiant/Sophos write-ups document this exact Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject pattern as an Akira signature, distinguishing it from the more common vssadmin.exe delete shadows used by most other crews.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Win32_Shadowcopy*Remove-WmiObject*" OR Processes.process="*Get-WmiObject*Shadowcopy*Remove*" OR Processes.process="*Get-CimInstance*Win32_ShadowCopy*Remove-CimInstance*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("Win32_Shadowcopy","Remove-WmiObject"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("Get-WmiObject","Shadowcopy","Remove"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("Get-CimInstance","Win32_ShadowCopy","Remove-CimInstance"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where (CommandLine has_all ("Win32_Shadowcopy","Remove-WmiObject"))
    or (CommandLine has_all ("Get-WmiObject","Shadowcopy","Remove"))
    or (CommandLine has_all ("Get-CimInstance","Win32_ShadowCopy","Remove-CimInstance"))
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Akira Ransomware Shadow Copy Deletion via PowerShell WMI
id: 8a1f6e2a-akira-shadow-wmi
status: experimental
description: Detects Akira (G1024 / Howling Scorpius / PUNK SPIDER) characteristic pre-encryption anti-recovery step using Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy piped to Remove-WmiObject (or Get-CimInstance / Remove-CimInstance variant), as documented in CISA AA24-109A.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/04/18
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.g1024
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_cmd_wmi:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Win32_Shadowcopy'
      - 'Remove-WmiObject'
  selection_cmd_cim:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Win32_ShadowCopy'
      - 'Remove-CimInstance'
  condition: selection_img and (selection_cmd_wmi or selection_cmd_cim)
falsepositives:
  - Rare administrative cleanup scripts; review parent process and account context
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\Pwsh.exe) (@CommandLine:(*Win32_Shadowcopy* AND *Remove-WmiObject*) OR @CommandLine:(*Get-WmiObject* AND *Shadowcopy* AND *Remove*) OR @CommandLine:(*Get-CimInstance* AND *Win32_ShadowCopy* AND *Remove-CimInstance*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(Get-WmiObject|Get-CimInstance)\\s+.*(Win32_Shadowcopy).*(Remove-WmiObject|Remove-CimInstance)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ucs.rationale: Most ransomware crews use vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet or wmic shadowcopy delete. Akira specifically and consistently invokes the PowerShell WMI/CIM pipeline (Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject) — CISA, Sophos and Mandiant tie this exact string to Akira intrusions across both the C++ and Rust (Megazord) variants. ucs.title: [LLM] Akira/Megazord mass file rename to .akira / .powerranges / .aki ransom extensions
ucs.description: Detects mass file-system rewrites where the resulting extension matches Akira's signature suffixes — .akira (original C++ build) and .powerranges (Rust 'Megazord' variant first seen Aug-2023), plus the .aki shortform used in newer 2024 builds. Combined with a >20 unique-folder count over a 5-minute bucket this catches the encryption stage cleanly with negligible benign overlap.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count values(Filesystem.file_name) as sample_files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as unique_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.akira" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.powerranges" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.aki") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user _time span=5m | where unique_paths > 20 | sort - _time
ucs.kql:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".akira" or FileName endswith ".powerranges" or FileName endswith ".aki"
| summarize UniquePaths = dcount(FolderPath),
            SampleFiles = make_set(FileName, 5),
            SampleProc  = any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            SampleCmd   = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleSHA256= any(InitiatingProcessSHA256),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where UniquePaths > 20    // empirical Akira encryption-burst threshold; benign single-file renames stay below
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".akira" or TargetFileName endswith ".powerranges" or TargetFileName endswith ".aki"
| summarize UniquePaths = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFileName, 5),
            SampleProc  = any(ActingProcessName),
            SampleCmd   = any(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where UniquePaths > 20
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*.akira OR @TargetFilename:*.AKIRA OR @TargetFilename:*.powerranges OR @TargetFilename:*.POWERRANGES OR @TargetFilename:*.aki OR @TargetFilename:*.AKI)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.(akira|powerranges|aki)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, UserName, bin(_time, 5m)], function=count(as=writes))
| writes > 20
ucs.rationale: The .akira and .powerranges extensions are unique to this actor's two binary lineages (original C++ build attributed by CrowdStrike to PUNK SPIDER, plus the 2023 Megazord/Rust rewrite). No legitimate software produces these extensions, so a single file is suggestive and a >20-path burst within 5 minutes is operationally definitive of Akira detonation. Pairs naturally with the shadow-copy UC above
